q2_gaps: Predicative sufficiency "X is (not) enough for Y": the Degree machinery covers "ADJ enough to V" and "enough / too much / too little + a quantity noun" only, so a bare predicative "enough" with a for-standard has no stated form — here it is encoded as an ordinary property class `enough` plus a preposition-named `For` oblique, which no rule licenses or forbids.

Cessation over a COPULAR state: the "no longer" recipe is written for events (state atoms + Past, then the same-symbol strength-0 And), so whether the reified state's flat copular twin is also emitted — and whether that flat twin needs its own matching denial — is unspecified; this parse emits the flat past positive with no flat counterpart in the denial.

Era/period adjective in the fuse-vs-split test ("modern ships"): the fusing list is term of art / nationality-origin / role title / material adjective and the non-fusing list is colour, size, damage, mood — "modern" falls in neither, so fusing to `modern_ship` (with the modifier genus, since "modern" is predicable) is undetermined.
notes: The cessation bundle is textbook — the same event symbol carries the Past positive and the Past-free strength-0 (And …) denial, with the definite port's typing and "old" projecting outside it, and "old port" correctly split as incidental description. The parse also correctly avoids the `forKind` comparison-class reading, since the ships are the standard of sufficiency rather than the port's own class.
